concept_uz: Kantorning xonasida cheksiz munchoq ramkasi: har qatorda oq va qora munchoqlar. Mehmon maqtanadi: «Hammasini roʻyxatga terdim!» Kantor diagonal boʻylab yurib, har qatordan bittadan munchoq oladi va rangini teskarisiga oʻzgartiradi — yangi ip roʻyxatda yoʻq. Burilish: cheksizlik ham bir xil emas ekan.

facts.claim: Qaysi toʻplam koʻp ekanini bilish uchun sanash shart emas — bittadan juftlash kifoya; kimda ortib qolsa, oʻsha koʻp
Natural va juft sonlar juftlanadi (1↔2, 2↔4, 3↔6…), hech kim ortmaydi — ular teng
Kantor barcha kasrlarni ham bitta roʻyxatga terib chiqish mumkinligini koʻrsatdi (izohdagi savolning javobi: teng)
Diagonal: 1-qatordan 1-raqam, 2-qatordan 2-raqam… har birini teskarisiga oʻzgartirsak, yangi ketma-ketlik har qatordan farq qiladi va roʻyxatda yoʻq
Demak 0–1 ketma-ketliklar natural sonlardan koʻp — cheksizliklarning ham pogʻonalari bor
Kantor bu usulni 1891-yilda eʼlon qildi; koʻp zamondoshlari rad etdi, ammo vaqt uni oqladi
«Hammasini roʻyxatga terdim» degan mehmon — oʻylab topilgan qahramon (matndagi «kimdir»)

lines.text: Hammasini roʻyxatga terdim! Birortasi ham qolmadi!

scenes.prompt: The stout gentleman with the monocle slaps the huge bead frame proudly; the beads rattle loudly along the endless rows. He booms in Uzbek with a loud, pompous, self-satisfied older male voice: "Hammasini ro'yxatga terdim! Birortasi ham qolmadi!" Silence. The bearded mathematician by the desk answers quietly in Uzbek with a deep, calm, gently amused middle-aged male voice: "Bittasi qoldi." The gentleman freezes. Audio: rattling beads, a ticking clock, gaslight hiss. No subtitles, no on-screen text.

lines.text: Georg Kantor, nemis matematigi. U cheksizliklarni solishtirmoqchi edi.

scenes.prompt: Slow push-in on the bearded mathematician at his desk with the blue and red marbles. An off-screen woman says in Uzbek with a warm, clear adult female storyteller voice: "Georg Kantor, nemis matematigi. U cheksizliklarni solishtirmoqchi edi." He looks up with a small smile and says in Uzbek with a deep, calm, gently amused middle-aged male voice: "Sanash shart emas. Juftlash kifoya." Audio: marbles clicking, a ticking clock. No subtitles, no on-screen text.

Close-up of his fingers sliding the marbles into pairs, one blue above one red, click, click, click, until six pairs stand neatly and one red marble is left alone at the end; he taps it gently. He says in Uzbek with a deep, calm, gently amused middle-aged male voice: "Kimda ortib qolsa — o'sha ko'p." Audio: crisp glass clicks, one last lonely click. No subtitles, no on-screen text.

lines.text: Natural sonlar va juft sonlar ham shunday juftlanadi. Hech kim ortib qolmaydi — demak ular teng!

scenes.prompt: The camera flies low and fast along the two endless rows of glowing stones, white above and golden below, each pair joined by its shining thread, on and on toward the horizon, never a stone left alone; the mathematician watches from the start. Audio: a soft rising musical shimmer, each thread chiming as we pass. An off-screen woman says in Uzbek with a warm, clear adult female storyteller voice: "Natural sonlar va juft sonlar ham shunday juftlanadi. Hech kim ortib qolmaydi — demak ular teng!" No subtitles, no on-screen text.

lines.text: Birinchi qatordan birinchi munchoqni, ikkinchidan ikkinchisini olaman…

scenes.prompt: The bearded mathematician walks slowly down along the frame, touching one glowing bead in each row, stepping one bead further to the right each time, following the slanting line into the darkness. Audio: one soft bell tone for each bead touched, footsteps on wooden floor. He says in Uzbek with a deep, calm, gently amused middle-aged male voice: "Birinchi qatordan birinchi munchoqni, ikkinchidan ikkinchisini olaman..." No subtitles, no on-screen text.

lines.text: Va har birini teskarisiga oʻzgartiraman: oqni qora, qorani oq.

scenes.prompt: The glowing diagonal beads lift out of the frame one by one, flip colour in the air, white turning black and black turning white, and thread themselves onto a new brass wire in the mathematician's hands, which he then holds up. Audio: a crisp magical flip sound for each bead, then a low resonant hum. He says in Uzbek with a deep, calm, gently amused middle-aged male voice: "Va har birini teskarisiga o'zgartiraman: oqni qora, qorani oq." No subtitles, no on-screen text.

lines.text: Har qatordan bittada farq qiladi. U roʻyxatda yoʻq.

scenes.prompt: The stout gentleman hurries along the rows with his oil lamp, holding it up to row after row, wiping his forehead; his monocle finally drops on its cord. He says in Uzbek with a loud, pompous, self-satisfied older male voice, now flustered: "Qani u? Topolmayapman!" The bearded mathematician says in Uzbek with a deep, calm, gently amused middle-aged male voice: "Har qatordan bittada farq qiladi. U ro'yxatda yo'q." Audio: hurried footsteps, the lamp's flame flickering, the monocle's tiny clink. No subtitles, no on-screen text.
